scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A service with many users
scenes.caption: Asha and Kabir move from protecting one account to designing a fictional college-festival portal. Students register, organisers manage entries and a supplier sees only the programme. A failure can now affect people who never made the unsafe decision.
scenes.dialogue: Who owns the risk for the whole service?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Map assets and actors
scenes.caption: The registration database, identities and gate availability are assets. Students, organisers, suppliers and the service provider have different roles. Requests cross trust boundaries from a browser into a server and then into stored data.
scenes.dialogue: A signed-in user is not automatically allowed every record.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Risk needs an owner
scenes.caption: Separate the harmful event, the weakness, the safeguard and the person responsible for checking it. Use the supplied likelihood and impact estimates to prioritise this exercise. A numerical score supports a discussion; it does not measure real risk precisely.
scenes.dialogue: Every priority needs evidence and an accountable owner.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Choose the access boundary
scenes.caption: A supplier signs in successfully but has no registration task. Should sign-in grant the supplier all records, should the team share one organiser password, or should the server restrict access to the supplier’s authorised purpose?
scenes.dialogue: Authentication and authorisation remain different checks.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A shared responsibility map
scenes.caption: Asha assigns an owner for registration access, a gate fallback and supplier permissions. The team records what could still fail after controls are applied. No individual promise removes the service’s need for tested safeguards.
scenes.dialogue: An owner checks the control and the remaining risk.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the system lab
scenes.caption: Complete the entry check, map actors and trust boundaries, then prioritise the supplied risks and owners. This module uses only synthetic records and offline models, with no school-system investigation.
scenes.dialogue: Design the service before assuming it is safe.
